summary: Provision time-bound, auditable readonly roles for Cloud Trace/Cloud Monitoring and AWS X-Ray across prod accounts for performance investigations
description:
Issue summary:
Provide a short-lived, auditable, least-privilege path for SREs and Performance Engineers to access tracing and monitoring data across production AWS accounts and GCP projects to troubleshoot latency regressions without granting broad IAM permissions.

Background:
When investigating cross-service latency spikes we frequently need read access to Cloud Trace / Cloud Monitoring (Stackdriver) for GCP services and AWS X-Ray / CloudWatch Logs for services running in AWS accounts. Currently engineers either request wide-scoped roles or must escalate to infra/SRE to run ad-hoc queries, which slows incident TTR. We want a standardized JIT readonly bridge with audit logging and automatic expiry.

Impact:
- Slower incident resolution due to escalations and handoffs.
- Risk of over-permissive temporary roles being granted ad-hoc without consistent audit trails.
- On-call fatigue and longer pages-to-fix cycles.

Request (what we want):
1) Provision an auditable, time-limited readonly role for GCP projects that grants: Cloud Trace Viewer, Monitoring Viewer, Logs Viewer. Role should be assumable via our existing JIT token broker and require MFA from the on-call principal.
2) Provision a corresponding IAM role for AWS prod accounts (us-east-1, eu-west-1) with permissions: xray:Get*, cloudwatch:GetMetricData, logs:GetLogEvents, logs:DescribeLogGroups, logs:FilterLogEvents. Role must require STS AssumeRole with external_id and short TTL (requested 4h max).
3) Add role chaining/policy so that audit metadata includes: requestor, justification, originating Slack channel/thread ID, and policy used.
4) Update the oncall runbook with steps to request and use these roles and include required post-use attestation.

Scope / Constraints:
- Only for members of oncall/performance-engineering group.
- Roles are readonly and must not include write/put/delete permissions.
- TTL capped at 4 hours; renewal requires a second explicit request.
- Must integrate with existing JIT infrastructure (INT-27840 and INT-9543 are related).

Security / Compliance considerations:
- Require MFA and SSO identity verification when assuming the role.
- All assume-role events must be routed to audit logging (Cloud Audit Logs + CloudTrail) and retained per compliance retention policy.
- Provide a CI/CD PR that adds the role definitions and policy documents for review and history.

Operational steps to implement (proposal):
- Step 1: Draft least-privilege IAM policies for GCP and AWS and post as YAML to infra repo.
- Step 2: Create Terraform module that provisions the roles in targeted prod projects/accounts and wires STS/external_id and condition keys for SSO/MFA.
- Step 3: Update JIT broker config to include new role ARNs/identities and map group membership.
- Step 4: Add a quick acceptance test: a dedicated test principal simulates assume-role and runs a small set of read queries.
- Step 5: Update runbook and announce to SRE + Performance slack channels.

Acceptance criteria:
- Engineers in oncall group can request and assume the role via the JIT broker and receive readonly access to tracing/monitoring for the requested timeframe.
- All assume-role events are visible in audit logs with requestor and justification metadata.
- No ability to modify/rename/delete trace or logs resources using the role.
- Terraform changes merged with code review and an infra PR created.

Expected timeline:
- PoC policy + PR: 2 business days.
- Terraform module + broker config: 4 business days.
- Runbook update + announcement: 1 business day.

Notes / links:
- Related infra PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1142
- Oncall tracing runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/123456/Oncall+Tracing+Debugging+Runbook
